goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Indexing [0]['id'] on the embed_category lookup crashes the migration whenever that setting was never persisted, which is the common case

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 — The uncategorized_category_id fallback is unreachable and would itself index [0] on an empty result because that hidden setting is only persisted after seeding

adjudication.rationale: Real defect in the migration: it does `execute(...)[0]['id']` for the embed_category lookup without checking whether the query returned any rows. If there is no matching row (e.g., embed_category unset/blank or not matching a category name), `[0]` will be `nil` and the migration will raise before reaching the `if category_id == 0` fallback, making that fallback effectively unreachable in the failure case. The fallback query also uses `[0]['value']` with the same risk if that row is absent, but the key verifiable issue from the diff is the unsafe `[0]` access and unreachable fallback when the first query returns no rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — DELETE FROM site_settings destroys the only copy of embeddable_hosts and embed_category even when the backfill inserted nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the migration, `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` runs unconditionally, but that’s consistent with the diff’s intent: both settings are removed from `config/site_settings.yml` and server locale text, and the application logic is updated to use the new `embeddable_hosts` table (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, per-host category via `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`). If the backfill inserts nothing because the old settings were blank/missing, deleting those deprecated settings does not break correctness—the new source of truth is the table, and the prior values are no longer used. Therefore the finding frames intended deprecation as a bug and is not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:2 — def change contains raw execute calls, so the migration is irreversible and rake db:rollback fails instead of dropping the table

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` defines `def change` but issues several raw `execute(...)` SQL statements (SELECTs, INSERTs, and a DELETE). In Rails, `change` migrations must be fully reversible; arbitrary `execute` calls are not invertible by the command recorder. On `rake db:rollback`, Rails will attempt to reverse the recorded commands and will raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` when it hits an `execute`, preventing a clean rollback (and potentially preventing the table drop from running).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The raw INSERT bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization and validation, so scheme/path hosts never match record_for_host and embedding silently breaks
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the migration uses a raw INSERT that bypasses EmbeddableHost normalization/validation, causing hosts with schemes/paths to not match the later bare-host lookup (record_for_host), breaking embedding. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about migrated data not being normalized and failing host comparisons.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Site-setting text is interpolated into SQL unescaped, so a host containing a quote aborts the migration or injects SQL

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old SiteSetting value for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into lines, and then builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL literal with no escaping/quoting helper, a value containing a `'` will break the SQL (migration abort), and a maliciously crafted value could alter the SQL. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — create_table with force: true silently drops the table and all its rows if the migration is ever re-applied

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly does `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will issue a DROP TABLE (if it already exists) before recreating it. That means if this migration is run against a DB where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., partially applied, manually created, or accidentally re-run), existing rows would be destroyed. This data-loss behavior is directly present in the diff and is a reasonable correctness concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:25 — Blank category falls back to uncategorized_category_id whose default is -1, writing a nonexistent category into a null: false column with no foreign key

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, blank `category_id` is set to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, but the claim that this setting’s default is `-1` is not established anywhere in the diff. The migration even reads `uncategorized_category_id` from the `site_settings` table as a real category id. Also, the DB column only has `null: false` (no foreign key constraint shown), so even if an invalid id were used it would not violate the column constraint. The proposed issue depends on external assumptions about the setting default and thus isn’t a verifiable problem from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:4 — No index or uniqueness constraint on host despite case-insensitive lower(host) lookups and a backfill that can insert duplicates

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.string :host, null: false` but does not add any index or uniqueness constraint on `host` (or `lower(host)`). Yet the model does case-insensitive matching via `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so duplicate rows differing only by case (or multiple identical rows) are possible and will make `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?` pick an arbitrary "first" match. The backfill in the migration inserts values directly from the old `site_settings` list (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no normalization/deduplication, so entries like `eviltrout.com` and `http://eviltrout.com` (or repeated lines) can produce duplicates. This is a real data-integrity/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16 — Embedding` is a fake `OpenStruct` resource with a hardcoded `id: 'default'` that only wraps `EmbeddableHost.all`, so an index action on the existing embeddable_hosts resource would delete the whole adapter/route/serializer/controller layer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce an `Admin::EmbeddingController` that builds an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, and the client route uses `store.find('embedding')` to fetch it. However, the proposed finding is essentially an architectural simplification suggestion ("you could use an index action on embeddable_hosts and delete this whole layer") rather than a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff shows incorrect behavior resulting from the hardcoded id or OpenStruct wrapper; it’s a deliberate way to expose a single embedding config resource at `/admin/customize/embedding`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update` renders exactly the same payload as `show` and mutates nothing, making the PUT route at config/routes.rb:139 a dead write endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb, both `show` and `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)`. The `before_filter :fetch_embedding` builds `@embedding` as an OpenStruct containing a fixed `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`. The `update` action performs no mutation/persistence of any kind before rendering, so the PUT route added in config/routes.rb (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) is effectively a no-op “write” endpoint that returns the same payload as `show`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — The `saveChanges` action is referenced by no template, so it is dead code feeding the no-op server update.

adjudication.rationale: In the new admin embedding UI, the only template added is `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`, which triggers actions `addHost` (via the plus button) and `deleteHost` (passed into the `embeddable-host` component). There is no button/helper invoking `saveChanges`, nor does the `embeddable-host` component send `saveChanges`. Therefore `admin-embedding.js.es6`’s `saveChanges()` action is not referenced by any template/component in this diff and is effectively dead code. Additionally, the server-side `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` just re-renders the serializer without persisting anything, so even if called it would be a no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4 — The `id`, `host`, and `category_id` methods only re-delegate to `object.<same_name>`, which the `attributes` declaration already does.

adjudication.rationale: In app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb, the serializer declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` and then defines `id`, `host`, and `category_id` methods that simply return `object.id`, `object.host`, and `object.category_id`. This is redundant, but it does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect—Ember/ActiveModelSerializers would already serialize those attributes without the explicit methods. It’s a minor cleanup/style nit, not a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:3 — before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` duplicates the filters inherited from `Admin::AdminController` and the route's `AdminConstraint`, and is repeated in app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:3.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` to two new controllers, but the claim that these filters are already applied by `Admin::AdminController` and/or the routing `AdminConstraint` is not verifiable from the provided diff (those implementations are not shown). Even if `Admin::AdminController` already defines the same filters, re-declaring them would at most be redundant/extra callback invocations, not a clear correctness/security defect demonstrated by this change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — category_fabricator.rb now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators, so both filenames lie about their contents.
config/locales/client.en.yml:2498 — The new `admin.embedding.edit` key is referenced by no template or JS file and is dead on arrival.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `admin.embedding.edit: "edit"` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`, and within the shown templates/JS the embedding UI references other keys (`admin.embedding.title`, `host`, `category`, `add_host`, `confirm_delete`) but not `admin.embedding.edit`. However, an unused i18n key is not a functional/correctness defect introduced by the code; it’s a minor maintenance nit (dead string) and could also be intended for future use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:200 — The `hydrated || []` fallback is unreachable because `Array#map` on line 197 always returns an array.

adjudication.rationale: In `_hydrateEmbedded`, when `m[2]` is truthy, `hydrated` is assigned from `obj[k].map(...)`. If that line executes successfully, `Array#map` always returns an Array (including `[]`), which is truthy, so `hydrated || []` will never use the fallback. The only failure mode is `obj[k]` not being an array (in which case `.map` throws and the assignment line is never reached), so the `|| []` does not meaningfully improve correctness. This is at most a redundant expression / minor cleanup, not a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — The new plural branch always runs `delete obj[k]` while the singular branch deletes only on a successful lookup (line 206), an undocumented divergence inside one helper.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:9 — categoryId` duplicates `host.category` outside the `bufferedProperty('host')` buffer, requiring manual seeding (line 26) and re-sync via the `Discourse.Category` global (line 38) and escaping `rollbackBuffer()` on cancel (line 58).

adjudication.rationale:
The diff does introduce a separate `categoryId` state alongside the buffered `host` string, but this is not a verifiable defect.

- `bufferedProperty('host')` only buffers the `host` field; keeping `categoryId` separate is a reasonable pattern because the chooser binds to an ID while the model has a relationship.
- Although `cancel()` calls `rollbackBuffer()` and does not reset `categoryId`, that does not create an observable inconsistency: when not editing, the template does not use `categoryId`, and when re-entering edit mode, the `edit()` action re-seeds `categoryId` from `host.category.id`.
- The post-save `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(...))` is an explicit UI update (so the badge can render immediately) and not inherently incorrect.

So the finding reads more like a design critique than a clear bug/correctness problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:12 — record_for_host` returns `false` for bad input but a record or `nil` otherwise, giving one finder three return types callers must guess at.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, `record_for_host` explicitly `return false` for malformed/blank input, but otherwise returns `where(...).first`, which yields an `EmbeddableHost` instance or `nil`. That means the method has three possible return values (false/nil/record) rather than the typical finder contract of record-or-nil. While current callers in the diff use `.present?` and `try(...)` (so they won’t crash), the finding is still a verifiable API/correctness issue because callers cannot rely on a consistent return type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — resources :embeddable_hosts` generates index/show/new/edit routes the controller never implements, so it should be scoped with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`.

Those extra routes would therefore dispatch to missing controller actions (raising an action-not-found error if requested), so scoping the resource to the implemented actions is a valid, verifiable issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-')` normalizes only the first underscore and bolts an ad-hoc naming fixup onto `basePath`, a code path shared by every model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Unguarded `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration when no `embed_category` setting row exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Host values are interpolated into raw INSERT SQL, so a quote in the value aborts the migration mid-upgrade.

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration copies prior SiteSetting values into the new table using raw SQL string interpolation:

```rb
records.each do |h|
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
```

If any existing `embeddable_hosts` entry `h` contains a single quote (`'`) (or other characters requiring escaping), the generated SQL becomes invalid and the migration will error, aborting the upgrade mid-migration. This is directly verifiable from the diff (no escaping/quoting is performed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — host.destroy` has no nil guard, so a stale DELETE returns HTTP 500 instead of 404.
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:11 — update` passes a possibly-nil record to `save_host`, returning 500 for a concurrently-deleted host.
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 — params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is dereferenced without checking the param exists, yielding 500 instead of 400.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, the code does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a client submits a malformed request missing the `embeddable_host` top-level key (or it is nil), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil[:host]`, producing a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx/validation error. This is directly verifiable from the diff at lines setting `host.host` / `host.category_id`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, 500ing before validation can return 422.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 — update` persists nothing yet returns 200, so operator changes are silently discarded.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, `update` indeed does not persist anything (it just re-renders `@embedding`, which is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). However, in this diff the only editable data in the new admin UI is the list of `EmbeddableHost` records, and those are created/updated/destroyed via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save(...)` / `destroyRecord()` from the component). The Ember template `embedding.hbs` has no “save changes” button invoking `saveChanges`, and the controller’s `saveChanges()` sends an empty update `{}` anyway. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`, so a failed DELETE surfaces no error to the admin.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` without any `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which explicitly `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 — obj[k].map(...)` throws a TypeError if any `*_ids` key is null, aborting hydration of the whole payload.

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-IDs branch runs when a key matches `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` and the optional `s` is present (i.e., `*_ids`). In that branch it unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If the server payload includes a `*_ids` key whose value is `null` (or any non-array), this will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'map' of null`, aborting hydration. There is no guard like `Array.isArray(obj[k])` or `obj[k] || []` before calling `map`, so the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:201 — The raw `*_ids` key is deleted even when every lookup returned undefined, silently losing the ids.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]` truthy) always executes `delete obj[k];` after mapping ids: `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []; delete obj[k];`. Since `map` always returns an array (truthy) even if every `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined`/`null`, the original `*_ids` array is unconditionally removed, unlike the singular branch which only deletes when hydration succeeded. This can silently drop the ids when hydration fails or is incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowers only the column, so mixed-case referers silently fail the allowlist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`, and it does not chain `.then/.catch`. However, within the provided diff there is no template/UI wiring that calls `saveChanges` (the new `embedding.hbs` only calls `addHost`/`deleteHost`), so the alleged lack of failure feedback is not a verifiable runtime problem introduced by this change. Additionally, the diff does not show what `embedding.update` returns or how it handles errors internally, so claiming a discarded promise causing missing feedback is speculative based on code outside the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Backfill is untested and `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError when no site_settings row matches 'embed_category'.

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does:

category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i

If that SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., no site_settings row for 'embed_category'), execute(...)[0] will be nil and ['id'] will raise NoMethodError before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13 — "raises an error with a missing host" arranges nothing and now passes only because referer is nil.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test "raises an error with a missing host" used to arrange the failure by setting `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`. That arrangement was removed, and the new production code no longer has a distinct "hosts not set" error; it only raises unless `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. The test still does `get :comments, embed_url: embed_url` without stubbing `request.referer` or creating any `EmbeddableHost`, so it now fails (and thus passes the expectation) simply because `request.referer` is nil, making `host_allowed?(nil)` false and triggering the "invalid referer host" path. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:86 — "works with a host with a path" is vacuous because before_validation strips the path down to plain 'example.com'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbeddableHost` normalizes `host` in `before_validation` by stripping scheme and any path (`sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`). In the updated `embed_controller_spec.rb`, the “multiple hosts” setup fabricates an `EmbeddableHost` with `host: 'https://example.com/1234'`, which will be saved as `example.com`. That makes a test about “host with a path” effectively a normalization/acceptance check, not a functional bug in the code under test. At most it’s a redundancy/coverage critique of the spec, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — Scheme/path stripping has no test asserting the stored value, and `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError on a nil host.

adjudication.rationale: The `before_validation` block in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice without guarding for `nil`. If an `EmbeddableHost` is instantiated without a `host` value (e.g., missing/blank params), this will raise `NoMethodError` before validations can add errors. However, the claim that scheme/path stripping has no test is incorrect: `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` includes tests asserting `eh.host` becomes `example.com` after validation for http/https and path trimming.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?", host)` never downcases the argument and no test exercises a mixed-case referer.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, record_for_host does `host = uri.host` and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. If `uri.host` contains any uppercase characters (e.g., Referer `http://EvilTrout.com/...`), the SQL becomes `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'`, which will not match rows where `lower(host)` is lowercase (and `lower(...)` always is). The code never normalizes the argument (e.g., `host.downcase`) before comparison, and the added specs only test lowercase referers, so this case-sensitivity bug is not covered. This is a concrete correctness defect (false negatives for mixed-case referers) visible in the diff.
